messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty P1 triggered for billing-usage-ingest-lag - 1813456789
incident-bot: Summary: consumer group 'metering-ingest-v2' lag > 2M messages for topic 'usage-events-prod' across 3 partitions. Alerting threshold breached (5m sustained).
pagerduty: Notification dispatched to oncall (team: eng-sre) and escalation policy level 1 -> 2
Amy Chen: acked and taking lead. I'm oncall.
Ben Ortiz: on it - what do you see?
Amy Chen: consumer group lag spiked ~04:12 UTC, retention headroom fine. consumer lag graph: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/usage/consumer-lag?orgId=1
Amy Chen: quick checks:
```
# consumer group lag summary
kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server kafka.prod:9092 --describe --group metering-ingest-v2
Group           Topic                          Partition  CurrentOffset  LogEndOffset  Lag
metering-ingest-v2  usage-events-prod           0          124567890      124987345      419455
metering-ingest-v2  usage-events-prod           1          98765432       100256789      2591357
metering-ingest-v2  usage-events-prod           2          110234567      111045000      810433
```
Amy Chen: lag mostly on partition 1 and 2. Consumers show stable heartbeats but throughput dropped (consumer CPU at 96% for one pod).
Maria Gomez: noticed a spike in long-running GC on ingest-worker-3 around the same time. logs: https://logs.redwood/ingest/ingest-worker-3/2026-03-14
Ben Ortiz: probable cause: a bad model eval job (large batch) was scheduled on the same node as a consumer causing CPU thrash. We saw batch jobs colocated on gpu-pool-analytics.
Amy Chen: immediate mitigation options: 1) scale up consumer deployment replicas 2) restart the affected pod 3) cordon node and move batch jobs.
Sam Kapoor: I'll prepare to scale replicas if you want to restart as a quick win.
Amy Chen: doing a rolling restart of metering-ingest-v2 pod set (controlled restart) on namespace prod-infra now. command: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/metering-ingest-v2 -n prod-infra`
eng-sre-bot: Rolling restart initiated by Amy Chen. 3 pods will restart with maxUnavailable=1.
Amy Chen: restart in progress - monitoring lag.
Ben Ortiz: pinging infra to check node allocation, cc @Billing Ops - heads up on potential delayed invoice processing.
Billing Ops: noted. which customers could be impacted? any enterprise invoices blocked?
Amy Chen: early estimate: invoices generated from the last 2 hours may miss ~1-2% of token events for heavy users; some large customers with bursty usage could see undercounting. We'll confirm after backfill.
Maria Gomez: restart completed for two pods, third stuck in Terminating (OOMKilled previously). Investigating container logs.
Amy Chen: found OOM spike from heap growth in ingest lib - increasing JVM Xmx helped in staging earlier but prod was on older config.
Sam Kapoor: scaling replicas x2 to reduce per-pod pressure. `kubectl scale deployment/metering-ingest-v2 --replicas=6 -n prod-infra`
eng-sre-bot: Scale event accepted. Desired replicas: 6 -> current 4 -> target 6.
Amy Chen: lag decreasing but still ~400k on partition 1. starting backfill worker to catch up (bounded rate to avoid downstream pressure). backfill command:
```
python tools/backfill_metering.py --topic usage-events-prod --start-offset 100200000 --end-offset 124987345 --rate 2000
```
Ben Ortiz: good. What about alerts / pager escalations? we should suppress noisy alerts while backfill running.
Amy Chen: suppressing alerting rule for 'metering-ingest-lag' for 30m to avoid spam. manual mute in PagerDuty and Grafana.
pagerduty: Alert suppression recorded by Amy Chen until 1813459189 (30 minutes).
Billing Ops: please create a temporary customer-impact note. we'll draft messaging if we need to notify customers.
Amy Chen: creating internal ticket: BLG-2451 with priority P1 - will attach impact summary and desired timeline.
Sam Kapoor: taking over primary on-call at 1813457100 (my shift). Amy — handing off live state: consumers scaled to 6, backfill started, lag down from 2M -> 150k, backfill ETA ~18 minutes, next action: monitor backfill rate and ensure storage writes don't fall behind.
Amy Chen: handing off. key diagnostics and runbook steps in BLG-2451. I will remain reachable for questions.
Ben Ortiz: noted. I'll follow up with infra to cordon the noisy node and move batch jobs to analytic-pool-2.
Maria Gomez: will open a follow-up PR to align JVM Xmx in prod via config map and add OOM alerting for ingest pods.
Billing Ops: initial customer impact assessment: 8 enterprise accounts with >1M tokens/hour showed discrepancies in preview logs; will verify once backfill finishes before deciding on email notification.
Sam Kapoor: backfill progress: 50% done, lag ~60k, ingestion throughput now stable at ~10k events/s.
Amy Chen: thanks. when backfill completes, we'll run aggregation reconciliation: run `metering-reconcile --since 2026-03-14T04:00Z --customer-list BLG-enterprise-list.txt`
eng-sre-bot: Backfill completed at 1813457305. final consumer lag < 1k.
Sam Kapoor: reconciliation queued and running.
Billing Ops: please hold off on external communications until recon results. if discrepancies >0.5% for billed window, we draft customer messages and possible invoice adjustments.
Ben Ortiz: created infra ticket INFRA-986 to cordon node and move batch jobs.
Amy Chen: incident timeline and actions: - 04:12 UTC: consumer lag spike -> pager fired - 04:15 UTC: Amy acked and started investigation - 04:18 UTC: rolling restart + scale started - 04:24 UTC: backfill started - 04:35 UTC: backfill completed, reconciliation running - 04:40 UTC: Sam takes over for monitoring and recon verification
Sam Kapoor: I'm staying on for next 30m to confirm recon results. Will hand off to next oncall once clean.
Ben Ortiz: great job everyone. please add a short postmortem draft to BLG-2451 with RCA and mitigations.
Billing Ops: logged BLG-2451 note and will prepare customer templates if needed.
Amy Chen: closing pager in PagerDuty (incident in progress but page resolved).
pagerduty: Pager closed by Amy Chen at 1813457389. Incident record created PD-2026-03214.
Amy Chen: final note: root cause likely resource contention from an ad-hoc batch job scheduled on node with ingest consumer; mitigation: scheduling isolation (taints/tolerations) for heavy batch jobs, autoscaling policies for consumers, and tighter OOM/jvm alerts. Will draft in postmortem. :white_check_mark:
